contextBoundaryNote: Pre-1941 events (1917 Bolshevik Revolution, 1918 Western intervention, and 1939 Nazi–Soviet Pact) provide background context only; Edexcel Option P4 strictly examines 1941–91.

root.label: Cold War, 1941–91
root.gloss: Fifty years of US–Soviet ideological rivalry, nuclear arms races, European and Caribbean crises, détente, and Soviet collapse from 1941 to 1991.

children.label: KT1: Origins of the Cold War
children.gloss: Key topic 1: The origins of the Cold War, 1941–58 — Grand Alliance summits, ideological rivalry, US containment, the Berlin Blockade, NATO, the Warsaw Pact, and Hungary in 1956.

children.label: 1.1 Early East–West Tension
children.q2Chain: Grand Alliance & ideology (1941–45) → Tehran, Yalta, Potsdam & US atomic bomb (1943–45) → Long & Novikov telegrams, Iron Curtain & Soviet satellite states (1946–48)
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Grand Alliance & ideology (1941–45) → Tehran, Yalta, Potsdam & US atomic bomb (1943–45) → Long & Novikov telegrams, Iron Curtain & Soviet satellite states (1946–48).

children.label: Grand Alliance & Ideology
children.gloss: The Grand Alliance united Britain, the USA, and the USSR despite deep ideological differences between the superpowers and conflicting attitudes of Stalin, Truman, and Churchill.

children.label: Capitalism vs Communist Rule
children.detail: Multi-party democracy and free markets clashed fundamentally with Stalin’s one-party command economy.
children.gloss: Multi-party democracy and free markets clashed fundamentally with Stalin’s one-party command economy.

children.label: June 1941 Wartime Coalition
children.detail: Hitler’s invasion of the USSR and Pearl Harbor forged a marriage of convenience backed by Lend-Lease aid.
children.gloss: Hitler’s invasion of the USSR and Pearl Harbor forged a marriage of convenience backed by Lend-Lease aid.

children.label: Delayed Second Front Mistrust
children.detail: Stalin suspected Churchill and Roosevelt postponed invading France until 1944 to bleed the Red Army.
children.gloss: Stalin suspected Churchill and Roosevelt postponed invading France until 1944 to bleed the Red Army.

children.label: Clashing Post-War Security Aims
children.detail: Stalin demanded a loyal Eastern buffer, whereas Truman and Churchill championed free democratic elections.
children.gloss: Stalin demanded a loyal Eastern buffer, whereas Truman and Churchill championed free democratic elections.

children.label: Masked Rivalry Until Victory
children.detail: Defeating Nazi Germany hid rival worldviews only temporarily, so alliance unity unravelled rapidly in 1945.
children.gloss: Defeating Nazi Germany hid rival worldviews only temporarily, so alliance unity unravelled rapidly in 1945.

children.label: Tehran, Yalta & Potsdam
children.gloss: Outcomes of the Tehran, Yalta, and Potsdam conferences shifted from wartime Second Front agreements to open clashes over Germany, reparations, and Poland.

children.label: Tehran (1943): France & Poland
children.detail: Roosevelt backed a May 1944 Normandy landing over Churchill’s Balkan plan and ceded eastern Poland.
children.gloss: Roosevelt backed a May 1944 Normandy landing over Churchill’s Balkan plan and ceded eastern Poland.

children.label: Yalta (Feb 1945): Four Zones
children.detail: Allied leaders split Germany and Berlin into four zones, set $20bn reparations, and pledged free elections.
children.gloss: Allied leaders split Germany and Berlin into four zones, set $20bn reparations, and pledged free elections.

children.label: Potsdam Clash Over Lublin Poles
children.detail: Anti-communist Truman challenged Stalin in July 1945 for arresting Polish democrats and imposing Communist rule.
children.gloss: Anti-communist Truman challenged Stalin in July 1945 for arresting Polish democrats and imposing Communist rule.

children.label: Divided Zone Reparations Deal
children.detail: With Attlee replacing Churchill, Potsdam let each power take reparations mainly from its own German zone.
children.gloss: With Attlee replacing Churchill, Potsdam let each power take reparations mainly from its own German zone.

children.label: Exposed Post-War Polish Split
children.detail: Losing a common Nazi enemy and Roosevelt’s diplomacy turned Big Three summits into open confrontation.
children.gloss: Losing a common Nazi enemy and Roosevelt’s diplomacy turned Big Three summits into open confrontation.

children.label: Atomic Bomb & 1946 Telegrams
children.gloss: Development of the atomic bomb and the 1946 Long and Novikov telegrams poisoned US-Soviet relations by convincing both capitals the rival sought dominance.

children.label: Aug 1945 Hiroshima & Nagasaki
children.detail: After July’s Trinity test hardened Truman at Potsdam, US atomic bombings defeated Japan without Soviet help.
children.gloss: After July’s Trinity test hardened Truman at Potsdam, US atomic bombings defeated Japan without Soviet help.

children.label: Kennan & Novikov 1946 Warnings
children.detail: Kennan’s Long Telegram urged firm containment, while Novikov warned Stalin that Washington sought world supremacy.
children.gloss: Kennan’s Long Telegram urged firm containment, while Novikov warned Stalin that Washington sought world supremacy.

children.label: Soviet Crash Nuclear Programme
children.detail: Seeing US atomic monopoly as intimidation, Stalin ordered Beria’s physicists to test a Soviet bomb by 1949.
children.gloss: Seeing US atomic monopoly as intimidation, Stalin ordered Beria’s physicists to test a Soviet bomb by 1949.

children.label: Washington Shifted to Containment
children.detail: Kennan’s dispatch ended hopes of post-war partnership and persuaded Truman’s cabinet to resist Soviet expansion.
children.gloss: Kennan’s dispatch ended hopes of post-war partnership and persuaded Truman’s cabinet to resist Soviet expansion.

children.label: Locked Both Sides Into Mistrust
children.detail: Nuclear fear and mirror-image diplomatic warnings framed every rival move as calculated Cold War aggression.
children.gloss: Nuclear fear and mirror-image diplomatic warnings framed every rival move as calculated Cold War aggression.

children.label: Iron Curtain & Satellite States
children.gloss: Churchill’s Iron Curtain speech condemned the creation of Soviet satellite states in Eastern Europe as Stalin installed loyal one-party regimes.

children.label: Stalin’s Security Buffer Goal
children.detail: Invaded twice through Eastern Europe, Moscow used Red Army occupation to install obedient Communist neighbours.
children.gloss: Invaded twice through Eastern Europe, Moscow used Red Army occupation to install obedient Communist neighbours.

children.label: Fulton Iron Curtain Speech (1946)
children.detail: Speaking beside Truman in Missouri, Churchill warned an Iron Curtain had descended from Stettin to Trieste.
children.gloss: Speaking beside Truman in Missouri, Churchill warned an Iron Curtain had descended from Stettin to Trieste.

children.label: Rigged Votes & Salami Tactics
children.detail: Secret police intimidation sliced away rivals across Poland, Hungary, Romania, and Bulgaria to build dictatorships.
children.gloss: Secret police intimidation sliced away rivals across Poland, Hungary, Romania, and Bulgaria to build dictatorships.

children.label: Feb 1948 Czechoslovak Coup
children.detail: Communists purged democrats in Prague, ending Eastern Europe’s last democracy and shocking US Congressmen.
children.gloss: Communists purged democrats in Prague, ending Eastern Europe’s last democracy and shocking US Congressmen.

children.label: Cemented Europe’s Bloc Division
children.detail: Breaking Yalta’s free-election pledge convinced Washington that Moscow was building an empire rather than defence.
children.gloss: Breaking Yalta’s free-election pledge convinced Washington that Moscow was building an empire rather than defence.

children.label: 1.2 Development of the Cold War
children.q2Chain: 1947 Truman Doctrine & Marshall Plan containment → Cominform (1947), Comecon (1949) & 1948 Berlin Blockade → Allied Airlift victory, FRG/GDR split & 1949 NATO
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: 1947 Truman Doctrine & Marshall Plan containment → Cominform (1947), Comecon (1949) & 1948 Berlin Blockade → Allied Airlift victory, FRG/GDR split & 1949 NATO.

children.label: Truman Doctrine & Marshall Plan
children.gloss: The 1947 Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan reshaped US-Soviet relations by ending US isolationism and funding European recovery against communism.

children.label: Britain Halted Greek Aid (1947)
children.detail: Bankrupt London ended support for royalists in Greece, prompting Truman to send $400m to Greece and Turkey.
children.gloss: Bankrupt London ended support for royalists in Greece, prompting Truman to send $400m to Greece and Turkey.

children.label: $13bn Marshall Recovery Programme
children.detail: Secretary George Marshall offered food, fuel, and machinery to sixteen Western European states to curb poverty.
children.gloss: Secretary George Marshall offered food, fuel, and machinery to sixteen Western European states to curb poverty.

children.label: US Isolationism Ended Permanently
children.detail: America pledged money and military backing worldwide to contain communism inside its existing borders.
children.gloss: America pledged money and military backing worldwide to contain communism inside its existing borders.

children.label: Stalin Denounced Dollar Imperialism
children.detail: Viewing US trade rules as economic warfare, Moscow barred Poland and Czechoslovakia from taking Marshall grants.
children.gloss: Viewing US trade rules as economic warfare, Moscow barred Poland and Czechoslovakia from taking Marshall grants.

children.label: Split Europe Into Economic Camps
children.detail: Prosperous Marshall-backed Western democracies pulled ahead while Stalin tightened economic control in the East.
children.gloss: Prosperous Marshall-backed Western democracies pulled ahead while Stalin tightened economic control in the East.

children.label: Cominform (1947) & Comecon
children.gloss: Stalin created Cominform in 1947 and Comecon in 1949 to enforce ideological conformity and integrate Eastern Bloc economies around Soviet needs.

children.label: Countering US Marshall Lure
children.detail: Stalin needed formal ideological and trade bodies so Eastern satellites could not drift toward American credit.
children.gloss: Stalin needed formal ideological and trade bodies so Eastern satellites could not drift toward American credit.

children.label: Cominform (1947) & Comecon (1949)
children.detail: Cominform directed Communist parties from Moscow, while Comecon coordinated state-planned trade across the bloc.
children.gloss: Cominform directed Communist parties from Moscow, while Comecon coordinated state-planned trade across the bloc.

children.label: Tito’s Yugoslavia Expelled (1948)
children.detail: Refusing Kremlin orders cost Marshal Tito Cominform membership as Stalin purged independent-minded Communists.
children.gloss: Refusing Kremlin orders cost Marshal Tito Cominform membership as Stalin purged independent-minded Communists.

children.label: Satellites Tied to Soviet Quotas
children.detail: Eastern states lost Western markets and supplied cheap raw materials and heavy goods for Soviet industry.
children.gloss: Eastern states lost Western markets and supplied cheap raw materials and heavy goods for Soviet industry.

children.label: Institutionalised Stalin’s Bloc
children.detail: Binding party loyalty and state trade under Kremlin control turned occupied neighbours into a sealed Soviet bloc.
children.gloss: Binding party loyalty and state trade under Kremlin control turned occupied neighbours into a sealed Soviet bloc.

children.label: Berlin Zones, Blockade & Airlift
children.gloss: Berlin’s division into zones triggered the Berlin Crisis of 1948–49, when Stalin’s land blockade failed against the Allied airlift.

children.label: Trizonia & New Deutschmark (1948)
children.detail: Merging Western zones and introducing a strong currency alarmed Stalin over a revived capitalist West Germany.
children.gloss: Merging Western zones and introducing a strong currency alarmed Stalin over a revived capitalist West Germany.

children.label: June 1948 Blockade & Airlift
children.detail: Stalin cut all road, rail, and canal links, so US and British planes flew 275,000 supply missions.
children.gloss: Stalin cut all road, rail, and canal links, so US and British planes flew 275,000 supply missions.

children.label: Stalin Reopened Access (May 1949)
children.detail: Unwilling to shoot down Allied cargo aircraft and risk nuclear war, Moscow lifted the blockade in defeat.
children.gloss: Unwilling to shoot down Allied cargo aircraft and risk nuclear war, Moscow lifted the blockade in defeat.

children.label: Western Prestige Boosted Globally
children.detail: Supplying 2.1 million West Berliners peacefully portrayed Truman as a defender of freedom against Soviet coercion.
children.gloss: Supplying 2.1 million West Berliners peacefully portrayed Truman as a defender of freedom against Soviet coercion.

children.label: Proved Containment Worked Safely
children.detail: Defeating Soviet pressure without firing a shot hardened permanent German division and sped up Western defence.
children.gloss: Defeating Soviet pressure without firing a shot hardened permanent German division and sped up Western defence.

children.label: FRG, GDR & Formation of NATO
children.gloss: The Berlin Crisis prompted the 1949 formation of the Federal Republic of Germany, the German Democratic Republic, and the NATO alliance.

children.label: Two Rival German States (1949)
children.detail: Trizonia formed the democratic FRG in May 1949 before Stalin proclaimed the Communist GDR in October.
children.gloss: Trizonia formed the democratic FRG in May 1949 before Stalin proclaimed the Communist GDR in October.

children.label: Twelve Nations Signed NATO (1949)
children.detail: Under Article 5, the USA, Britain, and ten allies treated an armed attack on one as an attack on all.
children.gloss: Under Article 5, the USA, Britain, and ten allies treated an armed attack on one as an attack on all.

children.label: Permanent US Troops in Europe
children.detail: NATO became America’s first peacetime military alliance, stationing US garrisons and bombers across Western Europe.
children.gloss: NATO became America’s first peacetime military alliance, stationing US garrisons and bombers across Western Europe.

children.label: German Reunification Hopes Ended
children.detail: Adenauer’s Bonn republic and Ulbricht’s East German regime locked Cold War fault lines across central Europe.
children.gloss: Adenauer’s Bonn republic and Ulbricht’s East German regime locked Cold War fault lines across central Europe.

children.label: Militarised Political Containment
children.detail: Turning economic aid into a nuclear-backed defence pact prompted Moscow to seek its own formal alliance.
children.gloss: Turning economic aid into a nuclear-backed defence pact prompted Moscow to seek its own formal alliance.

children.label: 1.3 The Cold War Intensifies
children.q2Chain: Superpower nuclear arms race & May 1955 Warsaw Pact → Khrushchev’s Secret Speech & October 1956 Hungarian Uprising → Soviet tank invasion, Kádár’s purges & muted Western response
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Superpower nuclear arms race & May 1955 Warsaw Pact → Khrushchev’s Secret Speech & October 1956 Hungarian Uprising → Soviet tank invasion, Kádár’s purges & muted Western response.

children.label: Arms Race & Warsaw Pact (1955)
children.gloss: The superpower arms race escalated from atomic to hydrogen bombs, while West Germany joining NATO triggered the formation of the Warsaw Pact.

children.label: H-Bombs (1952–53) & 1957 ICBMs
children.detail: After the 1949 Soviet A-bomb, both sides built thermonuclear warheads a thousand times stronger than Hiroshima.
children.gloss: After the 1949 Soviet A-bomb, both sides built thermonuclear warheads a thousand times stronger than Hiroshima.

children.label: May 1955 Warsaw Pact Created
children.detail: When rearmed West Germany entered NATO, Khrushchev bound seven Eastern satellites under unified Soviet command.
children.gloss: When rearmed West Germany entered NATO, Khrushchev bound seven Eastern satellites under unified Soviet command.

children.label: Europe Faced Two Armed Camps
children.detail: Rival NATO and Warsaw Pact commands entrenched Red Army garrisons legally across Eastern satellite states.
children.gloss: Rival NATO and Warsaw Pact commands entrenched Red Army garrisons legally across Eastern satellite states.

children.label: Nuclear Deterrence Curbed Direct War
children.detail: Fear of nuclear destruction made direct superpower war suicidal, deterring US force in Eastern Europe.
children.gloss: Fear of nuclear destruction made direct superpower war suicidal, deterring US force in Eastern Europe.

children.label: Raised Cost & Terror of Rivalry
children.detail: Huge missile budgets strained the Soviet economy while keeping Red Army tanks poised to police satellites.
children.gloss: Huge missile budgets strained the Soviet economy while keeping Red Army tanks poised to police satellites.

children.label: Hungarian Uprising & Nagy (1956)
children.gloss: Events in 1956 leading to the Hungarian Uprising saw Rákosi’s terror and Khrushchev’s Secret Speech spark protests and Imre Nagy’s radical reforms.

children.label: Rákosi’s ÁVH Terror & Speech
children.detail: Stalinist police terror and Khrushchev’s February 1956 de-Stalinisation speech sparked Budapest protests.
children.gloss: Stalinist police terror and Khrushchev’s February 1956 de-Stalinisation speech sparked Budapest protests.

children.label: Oct 1956 Riots & Nagy Appointed
children.detail: Students toppled Stalin’s statue on 23 October, forcing Moscow to name reformist Imre Nagy Prime Minister.
children.gloss: Students toppled Stalin’s statue on 23 October, forcing Moscow to name reformist Imre Nagy Prime Minister.

children.label: One-Party Rule & ÁVH Abolished
children.detail: Nagy freed political prisoners, ended censorship, and invited non-communist parties into a coalition cabinet.
children.gloss: Nagy freed political prisoners, ended censorship, and invited non-communist parties into a coalition cabinet.

children.label: 1 Nov Pledge to Quit Warsaw Pact
children.detail: Nagy declared Hungarian neutrality and appealed to the UN, crossing Moscow’s ultimate security red line.
children.gloss: Nagy declared Hungarian neutrality and appealed to the UN, crossing Moscow’s ultimate security red line.

children.label: Tested Limits of De-Stalinisation
children.detail: Leaving the military alliance threatened a dangerous gap in the Soviet buffer and forced Kremlin action.
children.gloss: Leaving the military alliance threatened a dangerous gap in the Soviet buffer and forced Kremlin action.

children.label: Khrushchev’s Invasion of Hungary
children.gloss: Khrushchev’s response sent 1,000 Soviet tanks into Budapest on 4 November 1956, crushing resistance, installing Kádár, and executing Nagy.

children.label: Fear of Satellite Domino Collapse
children.detail: Khrushchev feared tolerating Hungarian neutrality would spark copycat revolts in Poland and East Germany.
children.gloss: Khrushchev feared tolerating Hungarian neutrality would spark copycat revolts in Poland and East Germany.

children.label: 4 Nov 1956: 1,000 Soviet Tanks
children.detail: Red Army armour stormed Budapest against armed citizens, crushing two weeks of fierce street resistance.
children.gloss: Red Army armour stormed Budapest against armed citizens, crushing two weeks of fierce street resistance.

children.label: 2,500 Killed & 200,000 Refugees
children.detail: Heavy fighting devastated Budapest and drove 200,000 Hungarians across the Austrian border into Western exile.
children.gloss: Heavy fighting devastated Budapest and drove 200,000 Hungarians across the Austrian border into Western exile.

children.label: Kádár Purges & Nagy Executed (1958)
children.detail: Pro-Soviet János Kádár jailed 35,000 opponents, and Nagy was hanged in June 1958 as a bloc warning.
children.gloss: Pro-Soviet János Kádár jailed 35,000 opponents, and Nagy was hanged in June 1958 as a bloc warning.

children.label: Reasserted Iron Warsaw Pact Grip
children.detail: Brutal force proved peaceful coexistence never permitted Eastern satellites to leave Communist rule.
children.gloss: Brutal force proved peaceful coexistence never permitted Eastern satellites to leave Communist rule.

children.label: Hungary: International Reaction
children.gloss: International reaction to the Soviet invasion of Hungary brought outrage, aid, and boycotts, but nuclear risks and Suez prevented military help.

children.label: Nuclear Deterrence & Suez Split
children.detail: Eisenhower refused to risk H-bomb war over Hungary while Anglo-French intervention in Egypt divided NATO.
children.gloss: Eisenhower refused to risk H-bomb war over Hungary while Anglo-French intervention in Egypt divided NATO.

children.label: UN Outrage & $20m Refugee Relief
children.detail: Washington funded humanitarian aid and resettled tens of thousands of refugees after Radio Free Europe hopes faded.
children.gloss: Washington funded humanitarian aid and resettled tens of thousands of refugees after Radio Free Europe hopes faded.

children.label: Melbourne Boycotts & Party Splits
children.detail: Spain, Switzerland, and the Netherlands boycotted the 1956 Olympics as outraged Western Communists quit.
children.gloss: Spain, Switzerland, and the Netherlands boycotted the 1956 Olympics as outraged Western Communists quit.

children.label: Confirmed Unspoken Spheres of Rule
children.detail: Western military inaction emboldened Khrushchev that America would not fight inside the Soviet sphere.
children.gloss: Western military inaction emboldened Khrushchev that America would not fight inside the Soviet sphere.

children.label: KT2: Cold War Crises
children.gloss: Key topic 2: Cold War crises, 1958–70 — rising tension, flashpoint crises, and superpower reactions across Berlin (1958–63), Cuba (1959–68), and Czechoslovakia (1968–70).

children.label: 2.1 Increased East–West Tension
children.q2Chain: Berlin refugee drain, 1958 ultimatum & failed 1959–61 summits → 1959 Cuban Revolution, US embargo & 1961 Bay of Pigs → 1968 Czech opposition & Prague Spring
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Berlin refugee drain, 1958 ultimatum & failed 1959–61 summits → 1959 Cuban Revolution, US embargo & 1961 Bay of Pigs → 1968 Czech opposition & Prague Spring.

children.label: Berlin Refugees & 1958 Ultimatum
children.gloss: The acute refugee problem in Berlin prompted Khrushchev’s November 1958 Berlin ultimatum demanding Western troops leave within six months.

children.label: 2.7m East German Brain Drain
children.detail: Skilled doctors, engineers, and teachers fled Stasi rule through open Berlin into prosperous West Germany.
children.gloss: Skilled doctors, engineers, and teachers fled Stasi rule through open Berlin into prosperous West Germany.

children.label: Nov 1958 Six-Month Ultimatum
children.detail: Khrushchev demanded Allied garrisons quit West Berlin and turn it into a demilitarised free city.
children.gloss: Khrushchev demanded Allied garrisons quit West Berlin and turn it into a demilitarised free city.

children.label: NATO Refused to Abandon City
children.detail: Giving up West Berlin would have wrecked US containment credibility across Western Europe, forcing talks.
children.gloss: Giving up West Berlin would have wrecked US containment credibility across Western Europe, forcing talks.

children.label: East German Economy Near Ruin
children.detail: Continued youth flight threatened Ulbricht’s Communist showcase and pressured Moscow for a border fix.
children.gloss: Continued youth flight threatened Ulbricht’s Communist showcase and pressured Moscow for a border fix.

children.label: Reignited Flashpoint Over Germany
children.detail: Threatening East German control over Allied access routes pushed both superpowers into tense summit talks.
children.gloss: Threatening East German control over Allied access routes pushed both superpowers into tense summit talks.

children.label: Summit Meetings of 1959–61
children.gloss: The summit meetings of 1959–61 briefly eased tension at Camp David before the 1960 U-2 crisis and 1961 Vienna clash restored deadlock.

children.label: Geneva & Camp David Thaw (1959)
children.detail: Eisenhower hosted Khrushchev in September 1959, persuading Moscow to suspend its six-month Berlin deadline.
children.gloss: Eisenhower hosted Khrushchev in September 1959, persuading Moscow to suspend its six-month Berlin deadline.

children.label: May 1960 U-2 Wrecked Paris Talks
children.detail: After Soviet missiles downed pilot Gary Powers and Eisenhower refused to apologise, Khrushchev walked out.
children.gloss: After Soviet missiles downed pilot Gary Powers and Eisenhower refused to apologise, Khrushchev walked out.

children.label: Vienna Ultimatum Renewed (1961)
children.detail: Judging Kennedy weak after the Bay of Pigs, Khrushchev reissued his six-month Berlin threat in June 1961.
children.gloss: Judging Kennedy weak after the Bay of Pigs, Khrushchev reissued his six-month Berlin threat in June 1961.

children.label: Kennedy Hiked US Defence $3.2bn
children.detail: Refusing to yield Allied rights, Kennedy mobilised reservists while panicked Berlin departures surged.
children.gloss: Refusing to yield Allied rights, Kennedy mobilised reservists while panicked Berlin departures surged.

children.label: Closed Diplomatic Path on Berlin
children.detail: Two years of failed summits left building a physical barrier as Moscow’s only alternative to nuclear war.
children.gloss: Two years of failed summits left building a physical barrier as Moscow’s only alternative to nuclear war.

children.label: Cuban Revolution & Bay of Pigs
children.gloss: Impact of the Cuban Revolution: refusal of the USA to recognise Castro’s government and the Bay of Pigs incident forged closer relations with the Soviet Union.

children.label: Castro Toppled Batista (Jan 1959)
children.detail: Nationalising American land and oil refineries ninety miles off Florida ended US economic dominance in Cuba.
children.gloss: Nationalising American land and oil refineries ninety miles off Florida ended US economic dominance in Cuba.

children.label: US Embargo & Apr 1961 Bay of Pigs
children.detail: After Washington cut Cuban sugar and ties, 1,400 CIA-backed Brigade 2506 exiles were crushed in 72 hours.
children.gloss: After Washington cut Cuban sugar and ties, 1,400 CIA-backed Brigade 2506 exiles were crushed in 72 hours.

children.label: Soviet Sugar, Oil & Arms Lifeline
children.detail: Khrushchev bought Cuban sugar and shipped oil and weapons as Castro declared Cuba Communist in late 1961.
children.gloss: Khrushchev bought Cuban sugar and shipped oil and weapons as Castro declared Cuba Communist in late 1961.

children.label: Castro Accepted Nuclear Missiles
children.detail: Fearing a direct US military invasion, Havana welcomed secret Soviet medium-range launchers in May 1962.
children.gloss: Fearing a direct US military invasion, Havana welcomed secret Soviet medium-range launchers in May 1962.

children.label: Gave USSR Base Next to Florida
children.detail: Humiliating Kennedy encouraged Khrushchev to counter US Turkish missiles by placing warheads in Cuba.
children.gloss: Humiliating Kennedy encouraged Khrushchev to counter US Turkish missiles by placing warheads in Cuba.

children.label: Czech Opposition & Prague Spring
children.gloss: Opposition in Czechoslovakia to Soviet control over economic decline and StB censorship led Alexander Dubček to launch the 1968 Prague Spring.

children.label: Economic Slump & Novotný Ousted
children.detail: Falling Comecon living standards and brutal policing of 1967 student protests brought Dubček to office.
children.gloss: Falling Comecon living standards and brutal policing of 1967 student protests brought Dubček to office.

children.label: Apr 1968 Action Programme Reforms
children.detail: Seeking socialism with a human face, Dubček ended censorship, curbed StB arrests, and eased travel limits.
children.gloss: Seeking socialism with a human face, Dubček ended censorship, curbed StB arrests, and eased travel limits.

children.label: Uncensored Calls for Pluralism
children.detail: Despite Dubček’s Warsaw Pact loyalty pledges, new political clubs and Vaculík’s manifesto alarmed Moscow.
children.gloss: Despite Dubček’s Warsaw Pact loyalty pledges, new political clubs and Vaculík’s manifesto alarmed Moscow.

children.label: Eastern Hardliners Pressed Brezhnev
children.detail: East Germany’s Ulbricht and Poland’s Gomułka warned Czech free speech would infect their own one-party rule.
children.gloss: East Germany’s Ulbricht and Poland’s Gomułka warned Czech free speech would infect their own one-party rule.

children.label: Challenged One-Party Bloc Control
children.detail: Failed July–August summits convinced Brezhnev that even loyal Communist reform endangered the whole bloc.
children.gloss: Failed July–August summits convinced Brezhnev that even loyal Communist reform endangered the whole bloc.

children.label: 2.2 Cold War Crises
children.q2Chain: August 1961 construction of the Berlin Wall → October 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis quarantine & secret missile swap → August 1968 Czech invasion & Brezhnev Doctrine
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: August 1961 construction of the Berlin Wall → October 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis quarantine & secret missile swap → August 1968 Czech invasion & Brezhnev Doctrine.

children.label: Berlin Wall Constructed (1961)
children.gloss: The construction of the Berlin Wall on 13 August 1961 sealed the East–West border overnight with wire, concrete, and armed guards.

children.label: 40,000 Refugees Crossed in Aug
children.detail: Mass panic before expected border closure forced Khrushchev and Ulbricht to seal East Berlin immediately.
children.gloss: Mass panic before expected border closure forced Khrushchev and Ulbricht to seal East Berlin immediately.

children.label: 13 Aug Wire & Concrete Death Strip
children.detail: East German troops severed streets overnight and built a fortified 3.6-metre concrete wall around West Berlin.
children.gloss: East German troops severed streets overnight and built a fortified 3.6-metre concrete wall around West Berlin.

children.label: Families Split & Escapees Shot
children.detail: Refugee flight stopped abruptly, while guards shot would-be escapees like eighteen-year-old Peter Fechter.
children.gloss: Refugee flight stopped abruptly, while guards shot would-be escapees like eighteen-year-old Peter Fechter.

children.label: Oct 1961 Checkpoint Charlie Tanks
children.detail: US and Soviet tanks faced off 100 metres apart for eighteen hours before Kennedy-Khrushchev talks cooled it.
children.gloss: US and Soviet tanks faced off 100 metres apart for eighteen hours before Kennedy-Khrushchev talks cooled it.

children.label: Saved GDR Yet Shamed Communism
children.detail: Halting the brain drain rescued East Germany economically while proving communism locked citizens inside.
children.gloss: Halting the brain drain rescued East Germany economically while proving communism locked citizens inside.

children.label: Cuban Missile Crisis: 13 Days
children.gloss: Key events of the Cuban Missile Crisis took the world to DEFCON 2 before Kennedy’s naval quarantine and secret diplomacy averted war.

children.label: U-2 Photos & 500-Mile Quarantine
children.detail: After spy planes spotted Soviet missile sites on 14 October, Kennedy blockaded Cuba and Soviet ships turned back.
children.gloss: After spy planes spotted Soviet missile sites on 14 October, Kennedy blockaded Cuba and Soviet ships turned back.

children.label: Two Letters & 27 Oct U-2 Downed
children.detail: Khrushchev sent two rival peace offers as a US spy plane was shot down, bringing nuclear war hours away.
children.gloss: Khrushchev sent two rival peace offers as a US spy plane was shot down, bringing nuclear war hours away.

children.label: 28 Oct Deal Removed Cuban Sites
children.detail: Khrushchev dismantled Cuban launchers under UN checks in return for Kennedy’s public non-invasion pledge.
children.gloss: Khrushchev dismantled Cuban launchers under UN checks in return for Kennedy’s public non-invasion pledge.

children.label: Secret US Pullout From Turkey
children.detail: Robert Kennedy privately assured Ambassador Dobrynin that American Jupiter missiles would leave Turkey.
children.gloss: Robert Kennedy privately assured Ambassador Dobrynin that American Jupiter missiles would leave Turkey.

children.label: Closest Brush With Nuclear War
children.detail: Surviving Thirteen Days of brinkmanship scared Washington and Moscow into direct communication and treaties.
children.gloss: Surviving Thirteen Days of brinkmanship scared Washington and Moscow into direct communication and treaties.

children.label: 1968 Invasion & Czech Control
children.gloss: Overnight in August 1968, Warsaw Pact troops crushed Prague’s reforms, forcing the re-establishment of Soviet control in Czechoslovakia.

children.label: 20–21 Aug: 500,000 Pact Troops
children.detail: Forces from the USSR, Poland, Hungary, and Bulgaria seized Prague rapidly as Czech troops stayed in barracks.
children.gloss: Forces from the USSR, Poland, Hungary, and Bulgaria seized Prague rapidly as Czech troops stayed in barracks.

children.label: Passive Defiance & Palach Protest
children.detail: Unarmed citizens removed road signs, keeping August deaths under 100 before student Jan Palach’s sacrifice.
children.gloss: Unarmed citizens removed road signs, keeping August deaths under 100 before student Jan Palach’s sacrifice.

children.label: Moscow Protocol & Husák’s Purges
children.detail: Arrested Dubček was replaced in 1969 by Gustáv Husák, who purged 500,000 reformists under strict censorship.
children.gloss: Arrested Dubček was replaced in 1969 by Gustáv Husák, who purged 500,000 reformists under strict censorship.

children.label: Crushed Peaceful Communist Reform
children.detail: Twenty years of Husák’s normalisation extinguished hopes of democratic socialism until 1989.
children.gloss: Twenty years of Husák’s normalisation extinguished hopes of democratic socialism until 1989.

children.label: The Brezhnev Doctrine (1968)
children.gloss: Published after Prague’s invasion, the Brezhnev Doctrine justified joint Warsaw Pact force to preserve one-party rule across Czechoslovakia and the bloc.

children.label: Justifying Invasion Without Exit
children.detail: Because Dubček never tried leaving the Warsaw Pact, Brezhnev needed a rule outlawing internal reform too.
children.gloss: Because Dubček never tried leaving the Warsaw Pact, Brezhnev needed a rule outlawing internal reform too.

children.label: Sept 1968 Pravda Sovereignty Rule
children.detail: Moscow declared that threats to one-party Communist rule in any satellite endangered every socialist state.
children.gloss: Moscow declared that threats to one-party Communist rule in any satellite endangered every socialist state.

children.label: Ended National Satellite Freedom
children.detail: Eastern European regimes lost the right to allow rival parties or lift censorship for the next twenty years.
children.gloss: Eastern European regimes lost the right to allow rival parties or lift censorship for the next twenty years.

children.label: Invoked Again in 1979 Afghanistan
children.detail: Collective socialist intervention later gave Kremlin leaders ideological cover to send troops into Kabul.
children.gloss: Collective socialist intervention later gave Kremlin leaders ideological cover to send troops into Kabul.

children.label: Froze Eastern Bloc Until 1989
children.detail: Only Red Army tank threats kept unpopular satellite regimes in power until Gorbachev dropped the doctrine.
children.gloss: Only Red Army tank threats kept unpopular satellite regimes in power until Gorbachev dropped the doctrine.

children.label: 2.3 Reaction to Crisis
children.q2Chain: Berlin Wall lowers war risk & JFK’s 1963 speech → 1963 Hotline & Test Ban Treaty after Cuba → 1967–68 nuclear pacts & split reaction to 1968 Czech invasion
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Berlin Wall lowers war risk & JFK’s 1963 speech → 1963 Hotline & Test Ban Treaty after Cuba → 1967–68 nuclear pacts & split reaction to 1968 Czech invasion.

children.label: Wall Impact & JFK’s 1963 Visit
children.gloss: Impact of the construction of the Berlin Wall on US-Soviet relations lowered war risks, while Kennedy’s visit to West Berlin in 1963 scored a moral win.

children.label: June 1963 "Ich bin ein Berliner"
children.detail: Cheered by 120,000 citizens, Kennedy contrasted free democratic West Berlin with Communist concrete walls.
children.gloss: Cheered by 120,000 citizens, Kennedy contrasted free democratic West Berlin with Communist concrete walls.

children.label: Immediate Berlin War Risk Eased
children.detail: Stopping the refugee drain let Khrushchev drop his ultimatum while Kennedy noted a wall beat fighting a war.
children.gloss: Stopping the refugee drain let Khrushchev drop his ultimatum while Kennedy noted a wall beat fighting a war.

children.label: Lasting Western Propaganda Symbol
children.detail: Concrete watchtowers proved globally that Soviet-style socialism relied on force to keep workers inside.
children.gloss: Concrete watchtowers proved globally that Soviet-style socialism relied on force to keep workers inside.

children.label: Stabilised Europe’s Cold War Line
children.detail: Accepting divided Berlin defused Europe’s most dangerous flashpoint until citizens tore the Wall down in 1989.
children.gloss: Accepting divided Berlin defused Europe’s most dangerous flashpoint until citizens tore the Wall down in 1989.

children.label: 1963 Hotline & Arms Control
children.gloss: Consequences of the Cuban Missile Crisis included the 1963 hotline and attempts at arms control: the Limited Test Ban Treaty (1963), Outer Space Treaty (1967), and Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (1968).

children.label: June 1963 Direct Teletype Hotline
children.detail: Replacing slow crisis messages, an instant Washington–Moscow link let leaders defuse future emergencies.
children.gloss: Replacing slow crisis messages, an instant Washington–Moscow link let leaders defuse future emergencies.

children.label: Aug 1963 Limited Test Ban Treaty
children.detail: America, Britain, and the USSR banned nuclear weapon blasts in the atmosphere, outer space, and underwater.
children.gloss: America, Britain, and the USSR banned nuclear weapon blasts in the atmosphere, outer space, and underwater.

children.label: 1967 Space & 1968 NPT Agreements
children.detail: Superpowers barred orbital nuclear weapons and pledged not to transfer atomic technology to non-nuclear states.
children.gloss: Superpowers barred orbital nuclear weapons and pledged not to transfer atomic technology to non-nuclear states.

children.label: Khrushchev Ousted in Oct 1964
children.detail: Because America’s Turkish missile pullout stayed secret, Kremlin rivals removed Khrushchev over Cuba.
children.gloss: Because America’s Turkish missile pullout stayed secret, Kremlin rivals removed Khrushchev over Cuba.

children.label: Paved Way for 1970s Détente
children.detail: Establishing nuclear safety rules after Cuba built diplomatic habits that enabled SALT arms talks by 1972.
children.gloss: Establishing nuclear safety rules after Cuba built diplomatic habits that enabled SALT arms talks by 1972.

children.label: Czech Crisis: Global Reaction
children.gloss: International reaction to Soviet measures in Czechoslovakia paired muted US protest during Vietnam with deep splits across world communism.

children.label: 500,000 US Troops Tied in Vietnam
children.detail: Bogged down in Southeast Asia and fearing nuclear war, President Johnson avoided military intervention.
children.gloss: Bogged down in Southeast Asia and fearing nuclear war, President Johnson avoided military intervention.

children.label: Cancelled Summit & Vetoed UN Vote
children.detail: Washington scrapped planned Johnson–Brezhnev talks, while Moscow vetoed a UN Security Council condemnation.
children.gloss: Washington scrapped planned Johnson–Brezhnev talks, while Moscow vetoed a UN Security Council condemnation.

children.label: Eurocommunism & Communist Splits
children.detail: Romania, Yugoslavia, and China denounced the invasion as French and Italian Communists broke from Moscow.
children.gloss: Romania, Yugoslavia, and China denounced the invasion as French and Italian Communists broke from Moscow.

children.label: Shattered Soviet Moral Authority
children.detail: Invading a loyal socialist ally fractured global communism without stopping 1970s US–Soviet détente.
children.gloss: Invading a loyal socialist ally fractured global communism without stopping 1970s US–Soviet détente.

children.label: KT3: End of the Cold War
children.gloss: Key topic 3: The end of the Cold War, 1970–91 — 1970s détente and SALT treaties, Afghanistan and Reagan’s Second Cold War, Gorbachev’s New Thinking, the Berlin Wall, and USSR collapse.

children.label: 3.1 Détente in the 1970s
children.q2Chain: Vietnam costs, MAD fears & Soviet stagnation → May 1972 SALT 1, 1975 Apollo–Soyuz & Helsinki Accords → Human-rights strains & unratified June 1979 SALT 2
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Vietnam costs, MAD fears & Soviet stagnation → May 1972 SALT 1, 1975 Apollo–Soyuz & Helsinki Accords → Human-rights strains & unratified June 1979 SALT 2.

children.label: Détente & 1970s Tensions Eased
children.gloss: Détente and attempts to reduce superpower tensions in the 1970s grew from Vietnam War exhaustion, nuclear parity, grain trade, and Apollo–Soyuz.

children.label: Vietnam Drain & Soviet Shortages
children.detail: America faced $150bn Vietnam costs and inflation, while Brezhnev needed Western grain and technology.
children.gloss: America faced $150bn Vietnam costs and inflation, while Brezhnev needed Western grain and technology.

children.label: 1972 China Visit & Orbit Link-Up
children.detail: Nixon’s Beijing trip nudged Moscow into summits that peaked with the 1975 Apollo–Soyuz space handshake.
children.gloss: Nixon’s Beijing trip nudged Moscow into summits that peaked with the 1975 Apollo–Soyuz space handshake.

children.label: Expanded US Grain & Tech Trade
children.detail: Regular 1972–74 Nixon–Brezhnev summits unlocked American wheat shipments that eased Soviet food queues.
children.gloss: Regular 1972–74 Nixon–Brezhnev summits unlocked American wheat shipments that eased Soviet food queues.

children.label: Rivalry Continued in Third World
children.detail: Despite calmer European ties, proxy conflicts in the Middle East and Africa showed rivalry still simmered.
children.gloss: Despite calmer European ties, proxy conflicts in the Middle East and Africa showed rivalry still simmered.

children.label: Managed Rivalry Through Summits
children.detail: Pragmatic self-interest replaced 1960s nuclear brinkmanship with regular superpower summit diplomacy.
children.gloss: Pragmatic self-interest replaced 1960s nuclear brinkmanship with regular superpower summit diplomacy.

children.label: SALT 1 Treaty (May 1972)
children.gloss: Signed by Nixon and Brezhnev at Moscow in May 1972, SALT 1 capped ABM shields and froze strategic missile launchers for five years.

children.label: Two ABM Sites & Launcher Freeze
children.detail: The ABM Treaty limited defensive shields while an interim five-year pact froze ICBM and SLBM launchers.
children.gloss: The ABM Treaty limited defensive shields while an interim five-year pact froze ICBM and SLBM launchers.

children.label: Recognised Mutual Nuclear Parity
children.detail: For the first time Washington formally accepted the USSR as a strategic nuclear equal at summit talks.
children.gloss: For the first time Washington formally accepted the USSR as a strategic nuclear equal at summit talks.

children.label: MIRV Warhead Loophole Remained
children.detail: Omitting multiple independently targeted warheads let both arsenals keep multiplying destructive power.
children.gloss: Omitting multiple independently targeted warheads let both arsenals keep multiplying destructive power.

children.label: First Strategic Nuclear Cap Pact
children.detail: Slowing launcher construction proved arms verification could work despite ongoing technological loopholes.
children.gloss: Slowing launcher construction proved arms verification could work despite ongoing technological loopholes.

children.label: Helsinki Accords (Aug 1975)
children.gloss: Under the August 1975 Helsinki Accords, thirty-five nations agreed Three Baskets covering European borders, cooperation, and human rights.

children.label: 35 Nations Signed Three Baskets
children.detail: Ford, Brezhnev, and European leaders agreed deals on borders, economic-scientific trade, and civil liberties.
children.gloss: Ford, Brezhnev, and European leaders agreed deals on borders, economic-scientific trade, and civil liberties.

children.label: Basket 1 Recognised East Borders
children.detail: Western powers formally accepted post-1945 frontiers and East Germany, fulfilling a long Soviet goal.
children.gloss: Western powers formally accepted post-1945 frontiers and East Germany, fulfilling a long Soviet goal.

children.label: Basket 3 Empowered Bloc Dissidents
children.detail: Human-rights pledges inspired Charter 77 and Soviet watch groups to expose Communist police repression.
children.gloss: Human-rights pledges inspired Charter 77 and Soviet watch groups to expose Communist police repression.

children.label: Peak Détente Yet Eroded Bloc Rule
children.detail: While stabilising European maps, Basket 3 handed dissidents and Carter a moral lever against Moscow.
children.gloss: While stabilising European maps, Basket 3 handed dissidents and Carter a moral lever against Moscow.

children.label: SALT 2 & Strained Détente
children.gloss: Carter and Brezhnev signed SALT 2 in June 1979 to cap launchers equally, but human-rights disputes and Afghanistan killed ratification.

children.label: Carter’s Rights Push & SS-20s
children.detail: Carter angered Moscow by backing dissident Sakharov as Soviet SS-20 missiles and African moves alarmed hawks.
children.gloss: Carter angered Moscow by backing dissident Sakharov as Soviet SS-20 missiles and African moves alarmed hawks.

children.label: June 1979 Vienna 2,400 Cap Signed
children.detail: SALT 2 set equal 2,400 strategic launcher limits and placed first restrictions on MIRV missile systems.
children.gloss: SALT 2 set equal 2,400 strategic launcher limits and placed first restrictions on MIRV missile systems.

children.label: US Senate Conservatives Balked
children.detail: American critics charged that détente rewarded Soviet military build-ups in Angola, Ethiopia, and Europe.
children.gloss: American critics charged that détente rewarded Soviet military build-ups in Angola, Ethiopia, and Europe.

children.label: Withdrawn After Kabul Invasion
children.detail: Following December 1979’s Soviet move into Afghanistan, Carter pulled SALT 2 from Senate ratification.
children.gloss: Following December 1979’s Soviet move into Afghanistan, Carter pulled SALT 2 from Senate ratification.

children.label: Marked Collapse of 1970s Détente
children.detail: Shelving seven years of arms talks signalled the return of fierce superpower confrontation by 1980.
children.gloss: Shelving seven years of arms talks signalled the return of fierce superpower confrontation by 1980.

children.label: 3.2 End of Détente & Reagan
children.q2Chain: Dec 1979 Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, Carter Doctrine & Olympic boycotts → Reagan’s Second Cold War rearmament & 1983 SDI → 1985–88 Reagan–Gorbachev summits & INF Treaty
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Dec 1979 Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, Carter Doctrine & Olympic boycotts → Reagan’s Second Cold War rearmament & 1983 SDI → 1985–88 Reagan–Gorbachev summits & INF Treaty.

children.label: Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan
children.gloss: The December 1979 Soviet invasion of Afghanistan toppled Hafizullah Amin, killed détente, and trapped Moscow in a costly ten-year war.

children.label: Fear of Border Islamist Revolt
children.detail: After Amin seized power amid Mujahideen rebellion, Brezhnev feared Islamic unrest spreading into the USSR.
children.gloss: After Amin seized power amid Mujahideen rebellion, Brezhnev feared Islamic unrest spreading into the USSR.

children.label: Dec 1979 Troops Installed Karmal
children.detail: Soviet forces stormed Kabul, killed Amin, and backed Babrak Karmal using over 100,000 Red Army soldiers.
children.gloss: Soviet forces stormed Kabul, killed Amin, and backed Babrak Karmal using over 100,000 Red Army soldiers.

children.label: 15,000 Dead & $8bn Yearly Drain
children.detail: CIA-armed Mujahideen guerrillas bled Soviet finances and morale in Moscow’s own unwinnable Vietnam.
children.gloss: CIA-armed Mujahideen guerrillas bled Soviet finances and morale in Moscow’s own unwinnable Vietnam.

children.label: Global UN & Islamic Condemnation
children.detail: Invading a non-aligned Muslim state destroyed 1970s détente and united Western and Islamic states against Moscow.
children.gloss: Invading a non-aligned Muslim state destroyed 1970s détente and united Western and Islamic states against Moscow.

children.label: Exhausted USSR & Killed Détente
children.detail: Ten years of military failure weakened the Soviet economy and convinced Gorbachev to withdraw by 1989.
children.gloss: Ten years of military failure weakened the Soviet economy and convinced Gorbachev to withdraw by 1989.

children.label: Carter Doctrine & Boycotts
children.gloss: Washington answered Kabul’s invasion with the January 1980 Carter Doctrine, sanctions, CIA aid, and rival 1980 and 1984 Olympic boycotts.

children.label: Jan 1980 Persian Gulf Pledge
children.detail: Carter vowed US military force to defend Gulf oil routes, hiked defence 5%, and created a rapid force.
children.gloss: Carter vowed US military force to defend Gulf oil routes, hiked defence 5%, and created a rapid force.

children.label: Grain Embargo & Operation Cyclone
children.detail: America halted Soviet wheat and computer sales while channelling covert CIA weapons to Afghan rebels.
children.gloss: America halted Soviet wheat and computer sales while channelling covert CIA weapons to Afghan rebels.

children.label: 60+ States Boycotted 1980 Games
children.detail: Washington’s boycott spoiled Moscow’s 1980 Summer Olympics, prompting a 14-state Soviet boycott of LA in 1984.
children.gloss: Washington’s boycott spoiled Moscow’s 1980 Summer Olympics, prompting a 14-state Soviet boycott of LA in 1984.

children.label: Turned Rivalry Back to Containment
children.detail: Ending trade, treaties, and sporting ties buried détente even before Ronald Reagan entered office.
children.gloss: Ending trade, treaties, and sporting ties buried détente even before Ronald Reagan entered office.

children.label: Reagan & the Second Cold War
children.gloss: Ronald Reagan escalated the Second Cold War through trillion-dollar rearmament, Evil Empire rhetoric, and backing anti-Soviet insurgents.

children.label: $1 Trillion US Military Build-Up
children.detail: Reagan funded Trident submarines, stealth bombers, neutron warheads, and Pershing II missiles in Europe.
children.gloss: Reagan funded Trident submarines, stealth bombers, neutron warheads, and Pershing II missiles in Europe.

children.label: Mar 1983 "Evil Empire" & Doctrine
children.detail: Branding Soviet communism immoral, Reagan sent Stinger missiles and aid to anti-communist rebels worldwide.
children.gloss: Branding Soviet communism immoral, Reagan sent Stinger missiles and aid to anti-communist rebels worldwide.

children.label: 1983 Nuclear War Scares Peaked
children.detail: NATO missile deployments and fierce rhetoric raised Kremlin fears of a sudden American nuclear strike.
children.gloss: NATO missile deployments and fierce rhetoric raised Kremlin fears of a sudden American nuclear strike.

children.label: Ageing Kremlin Strained to Compete
children.detail: Matching high-tech American spending overwhelmed stagnant Soviet factories swallowing 25% of GDP.
children.gloss: Matching high-tech American spending overwhelmed stagnant Soviet factories swallowing 25% of GDP.

children.label: Forced Moscow to Bargain Later
children.detail: Negotiating from overwhelming economic and tech strength pressured Gorbachev to seek deep arms cuts.
children.gloss: Negotiating from overwhelming economic and tech strength pressured Gorbachev to seek deep arms cuts.

children.label: Strategic Defence Initiative (SDI)
children.gloss: Announced in March 1983, Reagan’s Strategic Defence Initiative (SDI) proposed orbiting anti-missile lasers that exposed Soviet tech weakness.

children.label: Orbiting "Star Wars" Laser Shield
children.detail: Reagan proposed space satellites to destroy incoming Soviet ICBMs before warheads reached US targets.
children.gloss: Reagan proposed space satellites to destroy incoming Soviet ICBMs before warheads reached US targets.

children.label: Threatened End of MAD Deterrence
children.detail: Kremlin planners feared a working shield would neutralise Soviet missiles and allow a US first strike.
children.gloss: Kremlin planners feared a working shield would neutralise Soviet missiles and allow a US first strike.

children.label: Exposed Soviet Microchip Lag
children.detail: Lacking advanced supercomputers and sensors, Moscow knew matching SDI research would bankrupt the USSR.
children.gloss: Lacking advanced supercomputers and sensors, Moscow knew matching SDI research would bankrupt the USSR.

children.label: Turned Tech Gap Into US Leverage
children.detail: Although unbuilt, SDI dominated Reykjavik talks and convinced Gorbachev the arms race was unwinnable.
children.gloss: Although unbuilt, SDI dominated Reykjavik talks and convinced Gorbachev the arms race was unwinnable.

children.label: Reagan & Gorbachev Summits
children.gloss: Reagan and Gorbachev succeeded in reducing tensions across four landmark summits, signing the 1987 INF Treaty before Malta in 1989.

children.label: Soviet Economic Decay & Chernobyl
children.detail: Swallowing 25% of GDP on defence amid 1986’s Chernobyl crisis forced Gorbachev to cut nuclear costs.
children.gloss: Swallowing 25% of GDP on defence amid 1986’s Chernobyl crisis forced Gorbachev to cut nuclear costs.

children.label: Geneva (1985) & Reykjavik (1986)
children.detail: Warm personal rapport built trust, even though Reagan’s refusal to drop SDI stalled sweeping cuts in 1986.
children.gloss: Warm personal rapport built trust, even though Reagan’s refusal to drop SDI stalled sweeping cuts in 1986.

children.label: Dec 1987 INF Abolished 2,600+ Arms
children.detail: Uncoupling SDI let both leaders ban all land missiles of 500–5,500 km range under on-site inspections.
children.gloss: Uncoupling SDI let both leaders ban all land missiles of 500–5,500 km range under on-site inspections.

children.label: 1988 UN Cuts & 1989 Malta Accord
children.detail: Gorbachev left Afghanistan and cut 500,000 troops before declaring Cold War rivalry over with Bush.
children.gloss: Gorbachev left Afghanistan and cut 500,000 troops before declaring Cold War rivalry over with Bush.

children.label: Replaced Arms Race With Real Cuts
children.detail: Personal trust turned freezing Second Cold War hostility into history’s first treaty destroying warheads.
children.gloss: Personal trust turned freezing Second Cold War hostility into history’s first treaty destroying warheads.

children.label: 3.3 Collapse of Soviet Control
children.q2Chain: Gorbachev’s New Thinking & dropping the Brezhnev Doctrine → 1989 Eastern European revolutions & fall of the Berlin Wall → 1991 Warsaw Pact end, August coup & USSR collapse
children.gloss: Q2 Narrative Chain: Gorbachev’s New Thinking & dropping the Brezhnev Doctrine → 1989 Eastern European revolutions & fall of the Berlin Wall → 1991 Warsaw Pact end, August coup & USSR collapse.

children.label: New Thinking & Loosening Grip
children.gloss: Impact of Gorbachev’s new thinking on Eastern Europe: Perestroika, Glasnost, and dropping tank intervention caused the loosening Soviet grip on Eastern Europe.

children.label: Perestroika, Glasnost & UN Speech
children.detail: Seeking to rescue socialism, Gorbachev eased censorship and told the UN in 1988 Soviet tanks would stay out.
children.gloss: Seeking to rescue socialism, Gorbachev eased censorship and told the UN in 1988 Soviet tanks would stay out.

children.label: Sinatra Doctrine Freed Satellites
children.detail: Abandoning the Brezhnev Doctrine left unpopular Communist regimes unable to crush democratic protests.
children.gloss: Abandoning the Brezhnev Doctrine left unpopular Communist regimes unable to crush democratic protests.

children.label: Poland & Hungary Broke Free (1989)
children.detail: Solidarity won June 1989 Polish elections while Hungary cut its Austrian border wire, opening refugee flight.
children.gloss: Solidarity won June 1989 Polish elections while Hungary cut its Austrian border wire, opening refugee flight.

children.label: Removed Force Prop From Bloc Rule
children.detail: Without Red Army intervention, forty years of Eastern European Communist dictatorships collapsed within months.
children.gloss: Without Red Army intervention, forty years of Eastern European Communist dictatorships collapsed within months.

children.label: Fall of the Berlin Wall (1989)
children.gloss: Mass East German protests and a bungled live broadcast triggered the fall of the Berlin Wall on 9 November 1989 and German reunification.

children.label: Hungarian Exit & Leipzig Marches
children.detail: Mass escapes via Hungary and 70,000-strong protests toppled Honecker once Gorbachev barred Soviet force.
children.gloss: Mass escapes via Hungary and 70,000-strong protests toppled Honecker once Gorbachev barred Soviet force.

children.label: 9 Nov 1989 Checkpoints Opened
children.detail: After spokesman Schabowski mistakenly announced immediate travel, crowds surged through and hammered the Wall.
children.gloss: After spokesman Schabowski mistakenly announced immediate travel, crowds surged through and hammered the Wall.

children.label: Domino Fall Across Czech & Romania
children.detail: Within weeks Prague’s Velvet Revolution elected Havel and Romanians overthrew dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu.
children.gloss: Within weeks Prague’s Velvet Revolution elected Havel and Romanians overthrew dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu.

children.label: Germany Reunified in NATO (1990)
children.detail: East and West Germany united peacefully under Helmut Kohl on 3 October 1990 inside the Western alliance.
children.gloss: East and West Germany united peacefully under Helmut Kohl on 3 October 1990 inside the Western alliance.

children.label: Shattered the Iron Curtain Symbol
children.detail: Ending twenty-eight years of divided Berlin visibly finished Cold War partition across the European continent.
children.gloss: Ending twenty-eight years of divided Berlin visibly finished Cold War partition across the European continent.

children.label: End of the Warsaw Pact (1991)
children.gloss: Democratic revolutions and the impending collapse of the Soviet Union proved decisive in bringing about the end of the Warsaw Pact in July 1991.

children.label: Elected Governments Rejected Moscow
children.detail: Non-communist leaders in Poland, Hungary, and Czechoslovakia demanded immediate Red Army troop withdrawals.
children.gloss: Non-communist leaders in Poland, Hungary, and Czechoslovakia demanded immediate Red Army troop withdrawals.

children.label: 1 July 1991 Alliance Dissolved
children.detail: Military structures closed in early 1991 before delegates in Prague formally ended the 36-year pact.
children.gloss: Military structures closed in early 1991 before delegates in Prague formally ended the 36-year pact.

children.label: Soviet Buffer Zone Disappeared
children.detail: Red Army garrisons pulled back eastward, ending four decades of Kremlin military control in central Europe.
children.gloss: Red Army garrisons pulled back eastward, ending four decades of Kremlin military control in central Europe.

children.label: NATO Left as Sole European Bloc
children.detail: Including reunified Germany, America’s Western alliance stood unchallenged as bipolar division vanished.
children.gloss: Including reunified Germany, America’s Western alliance stood unchallenged as bipolar division vanished.

children.label: Ended Military Division of Europe
children.detail: Dissolving Moscow’s alliance confirmed the USSR had lost superpower control outside its own borders.
children.gloss: Dissolving Moscow’s alliance confirmed the USSR had lost superpower control outside its own borders.

children.label: 1991 Coup & USSR Collapse
children.gloss: After Yeltsin defeated the August 1991 coup, republic secessions sealed the collapse of the Soviet Union and ended the Cold War.

children.label: Shortages & Baltic Secession Bids
children.detail: Perestroika queues and Glasnost nationalism led Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia to claim independence in 1990.
children.gloss: Perestroika queues and Glasnost nationalism led Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia to claim independence in 1990.

children.label: Aug 1991 Hardline Coup Defeated
children.detail: Communist plotters detained Gorbachev to block his New Union Treaty, but Boris Yeltsin rallied Moscow crowds.
children.gloss: Communist plotters detained Gorbachev to block his New Union Treaty, but Boris Yeltsin rallied Moscow crowds.

children.label: Dec 1991 CIS Replaced Soviet State
children.detail: Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus dissolved the USSR into the loose Commonwealth of Independent States.
children.gloss: Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus dissolved the USSR into the loose Commonwealth of Independent States.

children.label: Gorbachev Resigned on 25 Dec 1991
children.detail: Lowering the red Kremlin flag split the union into fifteen independent republics and ended Communist rule.
children.gloss: Lowering the red Kremlin flag split the union into fifteen independent republics and ended Communist rule.

children.label: Left USA as Sole Global Superpower
children.detail: Ending fifty years of US-Soviet ideological and nuclear rivalry closed the Cold War in Western victory.
children.gloss: Ending fifty years of US-Soviet ideological and nuclear rivalry closed the Cold War in Western victory.
